points.sujet: Net debt trajectory vs the <700 M€ target
points.ancienPropos: Q1 26 (07/05/2026, direct answer to a question on net debt, Nikita Papaccio Deutsche Bank): CFO Andrea Pazzi states that net debt is 'already below 700 M€, albeit marginally' at end-Q1, points to lower-than-usual Q1 capex having supported cash generation, and explicitly confirms the target of staying below that threshold for the full year, relying on 'the usual seasonality'.
points.nouveauPropos: H1 26 (29/07/2026): reported net debt comes in at 798,5 M€ at 30/06 - i.e. nearly 100 M€ above the level the CFO described as 'already reached, marginally' two months earlier. No analyst returns to the subject on the H1 call and management does not spontaneously address the gap with its own May statement, nor does it reconfirm the <700 M€ target for year-end in its opening remarks or in Q&A.
points.justification: Net debt is a central watch item for the thesis (anchor tension_dette_nette_non_tranchee, low confidence); the move from an explicit, quantified confirmation ('already below 700 M€') to an overshoot of nearly 100 M€ a single quarter later, with no reconciliation and no reconfirmation of the annual target on the following call, is a credibility signal to be tracked rather than smoothed over silently - the prudent modelling already retained in the file (target met by a narrow margin at year-end, low confidence) remains appropriate and is not changed by this observation.

points.ancienPropos: Q1 26 (07/05/2026, answer to Andrea Balloni Mediobanca on Q2 trends): Schillaci says that 'Q2 is showing a recovery, which is also reflected in our order book, globally and in China' and that, for European customers in China, 'in Q2 we are seeing an improvement, with a stronger order book' - a trend described as 'more positive vs Q1'.
points.nouveauPropos: H1 26 (29/07/2026): Schillaci describes China as having 'remained under pressure, with the market there facing some weakness after several years of growth', and specifies that performance was positive 'in all regions, excluding China, for market-specific reasons' - China is therefore explicitly excluded from the positive Q2 picture, with no link made to the 'recovery'/'improvement' in the Chinese order book announced two months earlier.
points.justification: Q1 26 flagged an anticipated recovery in the Chinese order book (overall and on the European OEM side) for Q2; the H1 call instead describes China as 'under pressure'/'weak' over that same Q2, with management not revisiting this divergence between the May expectation and the July observation - China is not a core driver of the thesis (margin of safety already embedded via the general prudence on omniumCA), hence a medium rather than high materiality.

clesRetenues: Q Martino De Ambroggi (Equita) - sector origin of the +3% cc guidance, volume/price mix assumption, level of prudence retained vs the pre-Gulf-conflict messaging (which pointed to +3% to +5%): Schillaci attributes the +3% mainly to volume/mix (motorcycles and aftermarket on top of auto), confirms that absent the geopolitical conflict guidance would have been +3% to +5%, and judges the +3% already 'significant and demanding' in the current context.

Q De Ambroggi (Sensify follow-up) - time horizon of the contribution (3 to 5 years?) and dry-dry/dry-wet architecture: Schillaci specifies an initial contribution from end-2026 and a main ramp-up in 2027 (so not a 3-5 year story), and confirms a natively dry-dry architecture (fluid-free).

Q De Ambroggi (follow-up) - is a second customer necessary for 2027 visibility, can the hundreds of thousands of units come from a single customer: Schillaci specifies that the key driver is platform volume (of the order of 100 000 units) rather than the number of customers, and confirms that the targeted volumes can be reached with the contracts already signed alone.

Q Monica Bosio (Intesa Sanpaolo) - confirmation that absent the conflict growth would have been above +3%, and clarification as to whether the first Sensify contract already generates the high volumes or whether it is the subsequent contracts: Schillaci confirms that reading, specifying that each signed contract covers roughly 100 000 units/yr, the contracts being homogeneous in that respect.

Q Bosio - M&A question on the Monroe Ride Solutions rumour (single target?, industrial/financial rationale, multiple threshold, dilutive effect): Schillaci declines any comment on market speculation, saying the group continuously reviews opportunities with nothing to share at this stage.

Q Bosio (follow-up) - would a broader system integration (suspension + Sensify + discs) be logical alongside the Sensify ramp-up: Schillaci refocuses on the current exclusive focus on the Sensify ramp-up and the already-existing 'corner' know-how.

Q Andrea Balloni (Mediobanca) - Q2 geographic trends, why the EBITDA margin is not raised despite the higher revenue, confirmation of the recovery in European premium volumes in China: Schillaci details a China Q1 down around 10% (incentive timing effect), expects a Q2 recovery in China and an improved order book at European customers in China; on the margin, he reiterates that holding 16,5% is already a demanding target given the volatility.

Q Nikita Papaccio (Deutsche Bank) - origin of the strong Q1 price effect and expected normalisation, reminder on Sensify's contribution/profitability, is net debt already below the annual target and will it stay stable: Schillaci explains a favourable timing effect between price adjustments and the trend in purchasing costs, not repeatable; declines to comment on Sensify profitability; Pazzi confirms net debt already below 700 M€ (marginally) at Q1, and confirms the target of staying below that threshold for the year, relying on the usual seasonality.

Q Papaccio (follow-up) - the aftermarket contribution was below 15% in Q1 vs a ~20% target for 2026, what drivers to move it up: Schillaci confirms ~15% in Q1, and expects progress towards ~20% driven by underlying growth (Asia, US) and by racing kits contributing more than expected.

Q Anthony Dick (Oddo BHF) - does Sensify involve several contracts with a single customer or several distinct customers: Schillaci confirms several contracts with several distinct customers, with discussions under way to broaden the customer portfolio further by year-end.

Q Dick (follow-up) - are the Sensify contract volumes validated by external forecasts (S&P etc.) given the past gaps observed on electrification: Schillaci acknowledges the risk already seen on electrification but stresses high visibility, since it rests on contract-by-contract contractual commitments over 4-5 years, the residual variability coming from the underlying market.
Q Dick (follow-up) - is the Sensify vehicle a 'conventional' vehicle: Schillaci declines to specify, saying only that 'it is a beautiful car'.

Q Dick (follow-up) - impact of the rise in the aluminium price on Q1 and on the rest of the year: Schillaci indicates aluminium is fully indexed to customers (a timing lag possible but manageable), impact not significant in Q1, more visible effect expected in the coming quarters.

Q Davide Zappa (Banca Akros) - is the +3% to +5% range still reachable if geopolitical tension eases in H2, drivers of the improvement in cost of sales (62% in Q1): Schillaci points to several possible scenarios depending on how the conflict develops (the +3% already being demanding), and will seize any opportunity if the backdrop improves; confirms an improvement in cost of sales of around 1,2-1,3 point tied to operational efficiency (Europe) and to raw material costs.

Q Alexandre Raverdy (Kepler Cheuvreux) - growth phasing (Q1 at ~2% organic), Q2 trends, acceleration expected in H2 with the new launches, is Sensify limited to autos or also LCVs/motorcycles, stance on bottom-up M&A deals vs larger transactions: Schillaci indicates a Q2 starting from a solid base consistent with the order book, confirms that the Sensify contracts signed to date cover passenger vehicles only (technology scalable over time to LCVs/motorcycles), and on M&A restates the absence of any update but the continuous monitoring of strategically aligned opportunities.

Q Michele Baldelli (BNP Paribas) - headcount target (~17 000 employees?), does Q1 capex (72 M€) point to full-year capex below the 350 M€ guidance: Schillaci confirms Q1 capex in line with the annual guidance (moderate acceleration expected), and attributes the increase in headcount (+3,6%, ~700 people) mainly to motorcycle market momentum in India and to new projects.

Q Anthony Dick (follow-up, 2nd round) - temporary profitability impact of the ramp-up of the new capacity (Mexico/China/Poland/Thailand) and of Sensify specifically: Schillaci details a ramp-up under way in Mexico (impact expected in H2), China already at a good production level, Poland (benefits visible next year), Thailand at a good level (motorcycles); on Sensify, he confirms a transitory negative impact typical of a ramp-up phase, expected to be absorbed quickly by 2027.

Q Martino De Ambroggi (follow-up, 2nd round) - is Brembo considering sourcing Sensify components from third parties, supply chain risks (semiconductors), update on coated discs: Schillaci indicates it develops all key components in-house (including the software) with no need for external insourcing, no continuity risk identified in the Sensify chain; on coated discs, several contracts already secured and SOPs already reached with some customers in connection with the November 2026 regulatory deadline (7 mg target), with growing interest from new customers.

Q Gianluca Bertuzzo (Intermonte) - origin of the confidence behind the guidance raise (was it excessive prudence at the start of the year?), order of magnitude of the net Sensify contribution from 2027 (2 or 3 digits in millions), maximum leverage targeted for M&A: Schillaci acknowledges having been 'probably too prudent' in March, confirms an 'interesting' Sensify impact from 2027 without further precision; Pazzi specifies current leverage of 1,1-1,2x with the capacity to go up to 2,0-2,5x.
Q Monica Bosio (follow-up, 2nd round) - current level of the capacity utilisation rate and recent trend: Schillaci confirms a stable level of around 86%.

Q Monica Bosio (Intesa Sanpaolo) - drivers of the better-than-expected Q2 performance (passenger cars finally positive), is the guidance raise tied to Sensify or to the organic trend, aftermarket growth in Q2, expected scale of the India motorcycle JV: Schillaci attributes the outperformance to a broad base (LCVs, motorcycles, passenger cars strong in North America/Europe), confirms that the +5% guidance raise is NOT tied to Sensify but to the organic trend and to a solid Q3 order book, Sensify generating a 2026 contribution but the significant impact still being expected from 2027; India JV opportunity estimated at ~100 M€ of total addressable revenue, captured share not yet quantified; aftermarket in line with Q1.

Q Bosio (follow-up) - does the CFO validate an analyst's estimate (100-150 M€ for Sensify 2027) or is it too conservative given the new customers: Schillaci indicates that the signed contracts cover platforms of more than 100 000 units each, says he 'hopes to be in that range, potentially higher', with the focus remaining on signing new contracts.

Q Andrea Balloni (Mediobanca) - why the full-year EBITDA margin is not raised despite revenue and a more favourable FX effect in H2, is mid-single-digit growth plausible over 2027-2028 with Sensify/coated discs, update on the new Sensify contracts since the last call: Schillaci describes holding the margin despite the raised revenue as a positive signal given still-significant ramp-up costs, declines to commit firmly on mid-single-digit growth in 2027-2028 (IHS market close to flat), confirms a twin driver (Sensify + coated discs + aftermarket) and strong Sensify commercial activity (RFI/RFQ) with new contracts expected in H2.

Q Martino De Ambroggi (Equita) - start-up timetable for Sensify production localised in China (homologation already obtained?), nature of the Q2 EBITDA bridge (-8 M€: Sensify/Greentell or the usual discs/calipers business), identification of the closest competitor in brake-by-wire: Schillaci breaks the bridge down into three specific factors (volume effect, ramp-up costs mainly Sensify, a one-off problem at one site generating undisclosed freight/logistics extra costs and expected to be resolved in H2), states he sees no competitor with technology comparable to Sensify, and indicates that the benefits of the China JV will be visible over the medium term.

Q De Ambroggi (follow-up) - is the site problem non-recurring (lower operating expenses expected in H2), amount of the one-off cost, net margin expansion expected in H2 given the higher revenue: Schillaci confirms a resolution plan in H2 that should narrow the gap but declines to disclose the amount of the one-off cost, and stresses that logistics costs remain an uncontrollable variable, making H2 margin expansion uncertain despite the raised revenue.

Q Nikita Papaccio (Deutsche Bank) - is the volatility in logistics costs tied to the Middle East conflict, drivers of the strength of the passenger cars segment in Q2 and H2 outlook, will the volume/mix dynamic stay strong if China declines less in H2: Schillaci confirms the direct link with the Middle East conflict, attributes the passenger cars strength to North America/Europe (beyond expectations) offsetting a China under pressure after several years of growth, and confirms that the favourable volume/mix dynamic is already embedded in the guidance.

Q Giovanni Selvetti (Berenberg) - is a Chinese customer among the new Sensify customers, where is the capex acceleration in H2 concentrated (350 M€ maintained vs 130 M€ in H1) and could the total ultimately be lower: Schillaci confirms an Asian customer among the new Sensify customers; Pazzi confirms that the 350 M€ capex guidance is maintained, with the acceleration mainly in Mexico and Poland, already embedded in the forecasts.

Q William Baker (Criseren Group) - expected trend in ROI over the coming years: Schillaci indicates an improvement expected via lower capex (the recent investment peak coming to an end) combined with EBIT growth.

Q Anthony Dick (Oddo BHF) - timetable for the next Sensify SOP among the contracts already signed, structural drivers of aftermarket growth (new capacity, new customers, new regions): Schillaci confirms a second SOP expected in 2027 (without specifying a quarter despite a follow-up), identifies China and North America as the key regional drivers of the aftermarket plus the broadening of the product range, with Sensify and Greentell cited as the main drivers of additional medium-term growth alongside the legacy braking technology.

Q Gianluca Bertuzzo (Intermonte) - clarification of the drivers of the guidance raise (surprising given the premium OEM warnings and the decline in global auto production), was Sensify already in the previous guidance, link to a specific region/product category, origin of the price effect in the bridge, are logistics costs included in the automatic customer adjustment mechanism: Schillaci reiterates that the raise is not tied to any specific region/category (aftermarket, OE Europe/North America, double-digit motorcycles driven by India, all growing), confirms that the price effect is tied to the rise in raw material costs, and specifies that logistics costs are NOT passed through to customers (managed internally, unlike raw materials).

Q Alexandre Raverdy (Kepler Cheuvreux) - H2 vs H1 reconciliation on the EBITDA margin (logistics costs, declining ramp-up costs), assumptions on raw material headwinds in H2 and timetable for recovery through the pass-through mechanism: Schillaci confirms that the rise in raw material costs is passed through with a structural time lag, will not be fully recovered by year-end (part of it readjusted only in Q1 2027), which explains keeping the margin guidance unchanged.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
World leader in high-performance braking. H1 2026 confirms the post-2025 rebuild: FY26 revenue guidance raised for the SECOND time this year (0% in March -> +3% cc in May -> +5% cc in July), Q2 accelerating (+6.4% published, 'almost 7%' cc), S1 +4.4% organic. The recovery is broad-based - North America/Europe passenger cars, commercial vehicles back positive, India motorcycles double-digit, aftermarket steady - and explicitly NOT driven by Sensify (impact 2027+). Margin guidance deliberately held at 16.5% EBITDA despite the top-line raises.

== THESIS READ ==
- Quality of the raise is high: broad-based organic improvement, not a single-program bet. Watch: H2 comparison base stiffens.
- Margin held flat on purpose (logistics, raw-material pass-through lag) - upside if those normalize. Watch: Q3 margin print.
- Net debt 798.6M vs the <700M target that was NOT reconfirmed - the balance-sheet tension is unresolved. Watch: FY guidance on net debt.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Published IFRS base, no retreatment needed. Sensify: 100-150M revenue range informally validated by the CFO as plausible ('potentially higher') - documented as SEMI-CORROBORATED upside but kept OUT of the central base. No sell-side consensus comparison available (basis null).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26 bottom-up: S1 actual 1,920.4M + H2 ~1,967M (+5% cc annual). EBITDA 16.5%, D&A ~285M -> EBIT ~356.5M (9.2% margin). Bridge: finNet -42M declining with deleveraging, ETR 28%; published 2025 reconciles at ~0 residual. 2027-2030: gradual margin rebuild toward ~10.5% EBIT, net debt to zero by 2030. Quarterly EPS detail: Q1 0.18 actual, Q2 0.19 derived, Q3/Q4 residual. Watch: Sensify first OEM quantification; FX drag (~2.3pts at H1, wider than assumed).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 results (Nov); Sensify OEM nominations/quantification; net-debt trajectory clarification; margin normalization on logistics.

ancrages.moteur: FY2026 guidance raised for the second time in 2026: +5% cc (vs +3% cc at Q1, vs 0%/in line with 2025 in March) - rebuilt bottom-up from actual H1 (1 920,4 M€) + estimated H2 (~1 967 M€, required to reach the annual guidance, implying an H2 acceleration vs H2 2025 of around +8%, plausible given Q2 already at +6,4% reported and the guidance raise itself).

EBITDA margin of ~16,5% held STABLE despite the raise to revenue guidance (confirmed twice in a row, Q1 and H1) - management continues to refuse to raise the margin despite the improvement in revenue, consistent with the creation anchor (Sensify ramping and new investments in Mexico/Poland/China absorbing the operating leverage).

MECHANISM CLARIFIED at this refresh thanks to the transcript: net debt 798,5 M€ at 30/06/2026, down 137 M€ over ONE YEAR (vs 935,5 M€ at mid-2025, consistent with the deleveraging thesis) but still above end-FY2025 (719,2 M€) and above the <700 M€ target for end-FY2026. H1 2026 free cash flow POSITIVE (73 M€), but H1 capex limited to only 130 M€ of the 350 M€ guided for the year (confirmed UNCHANGED by the CFO despite that slow pace, mainly Mexico/Poland) - implies a mechanical acceleration of around 220 M€ in H2 that will weigh on net debt before any improvement. No direct question asked on maintaining the <700 M€ target during the Q&A - status unresolved. Assumption retained on prudence grounds: <700 M€ target met by a narrow margin at year-end (690 M€), but LOW CONFIDENCE given the scale of the capex catch-up needed in H2.

UPDATED at this refresh: CFO Daniele Schillaci, presented with an analyst's estimate (Monica Bosio, Intesa Sanpaolo) putting the 2027 Sensify impact at between 100 and 150 M€, answers "we hope it will be in the range you mentioned, but potentially even higher" - a first INFORMAL validation of an order of magnitude, without however making a precise figure official (continued refusal to give firm guidance). Confirmation that the contracts cover platforms of more than 100 000 units each, that an Asian customer is among the new customers, and that a second SOP is expected in 2027 (quarter not specified). New China JV to localise Sensify at scale (not quantified). In line with the prudent methodology established at creation, NO Sensify value is injected into omniumCA/omniumEBIT beyond general growth - the 100-150 M€+ range remains documented as semi-corroborated upside but not made official, therefore outside the central base.

Gradual margin expansion continued over 2027-2030 (9,30% -> 9,80% -> 10,20% -> 10,55%), anchored on the historical pace of operational efficiency gains, in the absence of a quantified management target beyond FY2026, independently of any Sensify contribution - methodology unchanged vs creation.
Normative tax rate maintained at 28%, consistent with the recent effective rate, unchanged vs creation in the absence of any new element.

epsAdj.basisNote: No precise comparison with consensus available. The market reacted very positively (shares +11,1% intraday, +7,9% at the close) to the guidance raise. The transcript confirms that this raise is explicitly DISCONNECTED from Sensify - Schillaci makes the point twice in the face of similar analyst questions (Bosio, Bertuzzo): broad organic performance (passenger cars NA/Europe, commercial vehicles, motorcycles India, aftermarket) explains the raise, not an upward revision to Sensify expectations.

epsReported.note: No per-share figure disclosed in the H1 release/call; H1 26 net profit up 20.1% y/y (Q1 EUR 57M + Q2 EUR 61M, ~EUR 118M), Q2 net +30%. EPS to be anchored from the H1 report at next refresh.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No specific quantified quarterly guidance identified in the sources consulted for Q3/9M 2026.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026 guidance raised: revenue +5% at constant exchange rates (vs +3% cc previously); EBITDA margin maintained at ~16,5% (not raised); capex ~350 M€ maintained; net debt target <700 M€ maintained in the available sources but NOT explicitly reconfirmed post-H1 despite a level of 798,6 M€ at 30/06 (tension to be clarified).
pointsCles: FY26 guidance raised a second time this year (revenue +~5% at constant FX vs +3% previously), explicitly DISCONNECTED from Sensify per the CEO (stated twice to near-identical analyst questions): the driver is broad organic strength - passenger cars rebounding in North America/Europe, commercial vehicles back to growth, motorcycles double-digit on India, aftermarket steady - plus a solid Q3 order book; market reaction +8-11% on the day.

Sensify moved from story to industrial reality: serial production started in May for a leading global OEM, every signed contract covers platforms above 100,000 units/year (one Asian customer confirmed, next SOP in 2027, localization JV in China announced); confronted with an analyst's ~EUR 100-150M 2027 revenue estimate, the CEO 'hopes to be in that range, potentially even higher' - a first informal validation of the order of magnitude, with no formal guidance; CEO sees no competitor with comparable brake-by-wire technology.

EBITDA margin deliberately held at ~16.5% despite the revenue raise: Q2 bridge shows ~EUR -8M of 'operations' (volume effect, Sensify ramp-up costs, and an undisclosed one-off plant issue driving extra freight costs, to be resolved in H2), Middle East-driven logistics costs are NOT passed through to customers, and raw-material pass-through operates with a lag (part only recovered in Q1 2027).

Balance sheet strengthening: net debt EUR 798.5M (down EUR 137M y/y), H1 FCF +EUR 73M, FY capex ~EUR 350M confirmed (H2-loaded, Mexico and Poland) with ROI expected to improve as the investment cycle winds down ('harvest phase'); new mid-term levers: ABS-for-motorcycles JV in India (~EUR 100M addressable), Greentell, exclusive Superbike braking supply from 2027 with first carbon-ceramic discs in a production-derived series. Watch: the <EUR 700M net-debt target was not explicitly reconfirmed post-H1.
